body.statement: For sample sizes in the deterministic eventual regime \(\inf_{P\in\mathcal M}T_n(P)\ge T_0\), the sets \(\mathcal C_n(a)\) are intervals, and \(\Pr_P\{\theta(a)\in\mathcal C_n(a)\text{ for all }a\in J\}\to1-\alpha\) uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal M\). The image construction in \(\texttt{def:crossing-set}\) is therefore an eventual-regime simultaneous \((1-\alpha)\)-level confidence set for \(\tau_{\zeta}\) for every fixed \(\zeta\), including the empty and all-domain conventions.
body.justification: Joint LR calibration should report the scientifically interpretable crossing doses and the whole curve with one common coverage event.
body.gap: Doss (2026) reports pointwise LR intervals in the nurse-staffing application; the proposition uses a genuinely simultaneous LR critical value and a coverage-preserving inverse map.
body.consumer: The inversion map loses no coverage relative to the common LR event, but that event's nominal probability remains unproved.

obligation.what_is_open: The deterministic interval and threshold-crossing inversion is complete, but its claimed nominal limiting coverage is exactly the unresolved probability assertion in feasible calibration.
obligation.obstruction: Convexity and set-image arguments preserve coverage of the common LR event; they cannot prove that the proposed critical value gives that event the nominal limiting probability.
obligation.attempted: The constrained optimized value was proved convex, the simultaneous band event was identified exactly with the supremum event, and the true monotone curve was mapped to its threshold crossing under the stated endpoint conventions.
obligation.partial_result:
Fix \(k\in\{1,ldots,n\}\) and define
\[
 L_k(t)=\min_{v\in\mathcal C_n,\,v_k=t}
          \sum_{i=1}^n(Z_{(i)}-v_i)^2.
\]
The feasible set is nonempty because it contains the constant vector \(t\mathbf 1\).  If \(v^{(1)}\) and \(v^{(2)}\) are feasible at \(t_1\) and \(t_2\), then, for every \(\lambda\in[0,1]\),
\[
 \lambda v^{(1)}+(1-\lambda)v^{(2)}\in\mathcal C_n,
 \qquad
 [\lambda v^{(1)}+(1-\lambda)v^{(2)}]_k
 =\lambda t_1+(1-\lambda)t_2.
\]
Convexity of squared loss and passage to infima show that \(L_k\) is convex.  Therefore
\[
 Q_n(a,t)=L_{k(a)}(t)
 -\min_{v\in\mathcal C_n}\sum_{i=1}^n(Z_{(i)}-v_i)^2
\]
is convex in \(t\), and each sublevel set \(\mathcal C_n(a)\) is an interval, allowing the empty interval and \(\mathbb R\).  Positivity of \(\widehat\kappa(a)\) gives the exact event identity
\[
 \{\theta(a)\in\mathcal C_n(a)\text{ for every }a\in J\}
 =\left\{\sup_{a\in J}
          \frac{Q_n(a,\theta(a))}{\widehat\kappa(a)}
          \le\widehat q_{n,\alpha}\right\}
 =\{S_n(\theta)\le\widehat q_{n,\alpha}\}.
\]
On this event, \(\theta\) is an admissible nondecreasing selector by \(\texttt{ass:monotone}\), so the image in \(\texttt{def:crossing-set}\) contains its threshold crossing \(\tau_\zeta\), including the empty-set and endpoint conventions.  The inversion therefore loses no coverage relative to the common LR event.  It cannot determine that event's limiting probability; that is exactly the unresolved assertion in \(\texttt{thm:feasible-calibration}\).
